clue.text: Join in the main event before over, all ending

indicators.note: every word in the run contributes only its final letter, its ending

blocks.note: the last letters of these five words in turn

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to take part in the main bout before the contest is all over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Join in' reads as part of the sporting picture, but it is the definition; the rest supplies only word endings.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter a competition or activity is to take part, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Comprehensive finished shackling Oxford's principal

indicators.note: to shackle something is to hold it fast inside chains, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: through means done, finished
the principal (leading) letter of Oxford

explanation.surface: A thorough account of an Oxford college head being finally constrained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Principal' suggests a college head, a real Oxford title, but here it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorough survey is complete and detailed, so it is a close synonym of comprehensive.

clue.text: Help at the centre, tackling call — tough stuff

indicators.note: only the central part of the word is used, its middle letters
a tackler grabs and wraps round the opponent, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: the two middle letters of help
to call someone something is to name them

explanation.surface: Assistance in midfield making a tough tackle, a scene from a football match.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle pair of letters is split to go around the call word.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is the hardest substance in the body, coating teeth, so it is literally tough material.

clue.text: Get a grip with this immoral activity

blocks.note: first meaning: a bench tool with jaws that clamp work firmly
second meaning: wicked or depraved behaviour

explanation.surface: Advice to take control of a sinful habit.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests self-control over a bad habit; the first half is a workshop tool.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names both the clamping tool of a workbench and a moral failing such as gambling or drink.

clue.text: African country getting endless correspondence, legislation brought in

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter is dropped
something brought in is taken inside, so it sits within the other piece

blocks.note: correspondence is letters, mail
legislation makes law

explanation.surface: A southern African nation buried in letters while new laws are introduced.
explanation.walkthrough: The post word loses its final letter, then the legislation word goes in after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Malawi is a landlocked republic in south-east Africa, beside Lake Malawi.

clue.text: Get girl to imbibe say — from this?

definitions.text: Get girl to imbibe say — from this?

indicators.note: imbibing is drinking something in, so one piece takes another inside it

blocks.note: to win something is to get it
e.g. means for example, as does say
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Encouraging a young woman to have a drink, and asking what vessel she would drink from.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the vessel is what the girl would drink from.
explanation.definitionFit: A wineglass is a stemmed drinking glass, the natural thing to sip from when imbibing.

clue.text: Where one type of varnish may be applied, at once

definitions.text: Where one type of varnish may be applied

blocks.clueFragment: Where one type of varnish may be applied
blocks.note: first meaning: literally on a fingernail, where nail polish goes
second meaning: an idiom for paying immediately

explanation.surface: A manicure instruction about where varnish goes, done immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: To pay on the nail is a British idiom for paying promptly, in full.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means without delay, so it matches at once; literally it is the place for nail varnish.

clue.text: Quick blow, and I had cut

blocks.note: a rap is a sharp knock
I had cut short is the contraction I'd

explanation.surface: A sharp strike, and someone admits they had been wounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' tells you to shorten 'I had' to its contracted form, apostrophe dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid means fast or swift, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Warming thing in cake

blocks.note: a muff is a fur tube to keep the hands warm
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something heated inside a cake, as in a warm filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link to the definition but supplies its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A muffin is a small baked cake, either the British yeasted kind or the American sweet kind.

clue.text: Running backwards, easily beat old racehorse

indicators.note: going backwards means the letters are read from end to start

blocks.note: to murder an opponent is slang for to beat them easily

explanation.surface: A horse running the wrong way round the course still wins easily.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Rum was a famous British steeplechaser that won the Grand National three times in the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: Red Rum is a retired and long-dead racehorse, so old racehorse is a fair description by example.

clue.text: Schools etc used a complex

indicators.note: something complex is intricate and tangled, so the letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: the letters used for the shuffle

explanation.surface: Schools and similar institutions are using a multi-building site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complex' looks like a noun, a building site, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to teach or train them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Stop! Revolution won't change that

indicators.note: turning the word round end to end leaves it unchanged, so it reads the same both ways

blocks.note: an order to halt a vehicle or horse

explanation.surface: A cry to halt, insisting that no uprising will alter the outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' suggests politics, but it means turning the letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull up is to come to a halt, especially in a vehicle or on horseback.

clue.text: Glamour model, leg in the air

blocks.note: pins is slang for legs
up means aloft

explanation.surface: A glamour model posing with one leg raised.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin-up is a photograph of an attractive person, or the model in it, meant to be pinned on a wall.

clue.text: Admitting suffering, cook ruffled

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece takes the other inside

blocks.note: ill means unwell, suffering
to fry is to cook

explanation.surface: A cook, flustered, confesses to feeling unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruffled' tempts as flustered, but it means decorated with ruffles.
explanation.definitionFit: Frilly clothing is trimmed with frills, which are gathered ruffles of fabric.

clue.text: Range so old, time for a change

indicators.note: a change of arrangement means the letters are reordered

blocks.note: the letters used for the shuffle

explanation.surface: A worn-out range, perhaps of goods, is overdue for replacement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' reads as a product line, but it is a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dolomites are a mountain range in north-east Italy, part of the Alps.

clue.text: Upmarket pound shop!

indicators.note: to pound something is to batter it out of shape, so the letters are knocked into a new order

blocks.note: the letters used for the shuffle

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a cheap pound shop is surprisingly upmarket.
explanation.walkthrough: A pound shop is a British discount store where everything costs a pound; here 'pound' is a verb, batter.
explanation.definitionFit: Posh means smart and upper-class, a near synonym of upmarket.

clue.text: Collection of works ending in attic, author unknown

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of attic
anon. marks a work whose author is unknown

explanation.surface: A body of writings found in an attic by an anonymous writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is the accepted body of a writer's works, or of significant literature generally.

clue.text: Trick required to cross unspecified gorge

indicators.note: one piece must span over the other, so it wraps around it

blocks.note: a con is a swindle
any means no particular one

explanation.surface: A stunt involving crossing some unnamed ravine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gorge' could be a verb, to eat greedily; here it is a ravine.
explanation.definitionFit: A canyon is a deep, narrow valley with steep sides, the same as a gorge.

clue.text: Merited, by a whisker

blocks.note: first meaning: deserved, fair
second meaning: barely

explanation.surface: A victory that was deserved, though only narrowly won.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means fair and deserved; the adverb means narrowly or barely.

clue.text: Caribbean breakfast food: a tin one has opened

indicators.note: to open something here is to stand at its start, placed ahead of it

blocks.note: jam is spread on breakfast toast
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: A Caribbean breakfast item that someone has opened from a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: The numeral goes at the front of the tin word, which it opens.
explanation.definitionFit: Jamaican describes someone or something from Jamaica, an island in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Relative wants us to invest in currency

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: coin is money, currency
taken as written

explanation.surface: A family member asks us to put money into foreign currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A cousin is a child of one's aunt or uncle, a family relative.

clue.text: It's a religion this, no messing about!

indicators.note: messing about means fooling around with something, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters used for the shuffle

explanation.surface: A stern reminder that faith is serious, not to be trifled with.
explanation.definitionFit: Shinto is the indigenous religion of Japan, centred on the worship of kami.

clue.text: Country in North America embraced by both parents

indicators.note: something embraced is held in arms, so it sits inside the other pieces

blocks.note: pa is a father, one of both parents
NA abbreviates North America
ma is a mother, the other parent

explanation.surface: A country in North America hugged by a mother and father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Both parents' supplies the father and mother words either side; 'North America' is not the definition but an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Panama is a Central American republic, famous for its canal.

clue.text: Fine, light touch, heavy weight being lifted

indicators.note: lifted up in a down entry means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: a dab is a light touch
a ton is a heavy unit of weight

explanation.surface: A weightlifting scene where a heavy load is raised lightly and fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is not bad is a mild British way to call it fine or acceptable.

clue.text: Amount of money set aside, don't go under

blocks.note: first meaning: a sum kept in a till for giving change
second meaning: stay on the surface of water, an imperative

explanation.surface: Advice to keep a cash reserve so a business does not go bankrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go under' suggests business failure, but it means sink.
explanation.definitionFit: A float is the starting cash in a till; to float is to stay up on water rather than sink.

clue.text: Get on horse at the start, it repeatedly getting away

indicators.note: only the start of the word, its first letter, is used
repeated means given twice, so the word appears two times in a row

blocks.note: the first letter of horse
taken as written
taken again as written
off means away, gone

explanation.surface: Mount a horse at the start of a race and it bolts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get on horse' looks like mounting, but 'Get on' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people who hit it off get on well together, an idiom for instant rapport.

clue.text: Sell game that's on the up

indicators.note: going up in a down entry means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: golf is a game

explanation.surface: Selling off a sport that is growing in popularity.
explanation.walkthrough: To flog is British slang for to sell.
explanation.definitionFit: Flog is informal British slang meaning to sell, often hard or cheaply.

clue.text: Layered dessert, nothing much

blocks.note: first meaning: sponge, fruit, custard and cream in layers
second meaning: something of little value or importance

explanation.surface: A modest layered pudding that is no great thing.
explanation.walkthrough: A trifle is a classic British pudding of sponge, jelly or fruit, custard and cream.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names both the layered pudding and a thing of small importance.

clue.text: Soaked up by escalope, stonking sauce

indicators.note: something soaked up is absorbed inside, so the letters lie within the words that follow

blocks.note: found across the join of these two words

explanation.surface: A cracking sauce absorbed by a breaded escalope.
explanation.walkthrough: Stonking is British slang for excellent or huge.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is an Italian sauce of basil, pine nuts, garlic, oil and cheese.

clue.text: Turn hand, getting fly off the handle

blocks.note: a go is a turn in a game
a hand is a bunch of bananas

explanation.surface: A card player takes a turn, is dealt a hand and loses their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand' looks like cards, but a cluster of bananas growing together is called a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for losing one's temper suddenly, becoming wildly angry.
